steps.title: Prepare buffers and stock solutions
steps.instruction: Make all required buffers and stock solutions at the concentrations listed in the Recipes section.

substeps.instruction: Storage buffer: 20 mM HEPES pH 7.5, 100 mM KCl, bring to 50 mL with deionized water.
Buffer IN: 20 mM HEPES pH 7.0, 100 mM KCl, bring to 50 mL with water.
Buffer IN with fluorophore (5 mL): 20 mM HEPES pH 7.0, 0.1 mL 100 mM KCl, add either 250 µM Calcein, 100 µM Fura‑2, or 400 µM Magnesium Green, fill to 5 mL with water. Keep solutions light‑protected.
Buffer OUT: 20 mM HEPES pH 7.0, 100 mM NaCl, bring to 50 mL with water.
Ionophore stock (500 µM): dilute a 5 mM stock in 100 % EtOH 1:10; keep 10 µM working stock in 100 % EtOH (store –20 °C).
ACMA stock: dissolve ACMA to 10 mM in 80 % EtOH (store 4 °C); dilute to 1 mM in 20 % EtOH for use (store 4 °C).
Metal ion stocks (0.5 M, 5 mL each): MnCl₂·4H₂O – 0.49 g; MgCl₂·6H₂O – 0.51 g; CaCl₂·2H₂O – 0.37 g in deionized water. Prepare fresh for each experiment.

steps.title: Form lipid film and dry
steps.instruction: Create a thin lipid film of the desired POPE:POPG (3:1) mixture and dry it completely.

substeps.instruction: Pool 400 mg of lipids (≈16 mL chloroform) into a 500 mL round‑bottom flask; wash each lipid vial with chloroform and add the wash to the same flask (total ≈20 mL chloroform).
Evaporate chloroform with a gentle nitrogen stream while rotating the flask until a dry film forms; the stream should be felt lightly on nitrile‑gloved hands.
Wash the film with 20 mL diethyl ether, repeat nitrogen drying, then continue drying under nitrogen for an additional 20–30 min.
Exchange the nitrogen/air atmosphere in the flask with argon (use a desiccator).

steps.title: Solubilize lipids and extrude
steps.instruction: Resuspend the dried film, solubilize by sonication, freeze‑thaw, and extrude to obtain uniform vesicles.

substeps.instruction: Add 10 mL storage buffer to the flask and sonicate (15 s sonication, 45 s on ice) repeatedly until the lipids are fully solubilized (final concentration 40 mg/mL).
Freeze‑thaw the suspension with liquid nitrogen at least three times, thawing to room temperature each time.
Extrude the suspension through a 400 nm polycarbonate filter at least 11 times; keep the extruded lipids at >22 °C.

steps.title: Dilute lipids and destabilize vesicles
steps.instruction: Adjust lipid concentration for reconstitution and partially solubilize vesicles with Triton X‑100.

substeps.instruction: Dilute the extruded lipids to 4 mg/mL with storage buffer (5 mL total, room temperature).

Add 10 % Triton X‑100 (10 µL per 5 mL) while stirring and monitor absorbance at 540 nm (R_sat). When R_sat reaches its maximum and begins to decline, wait 30 s, then add a second 10 µL aliquot. Repeat for a total of five additions, each followed by a 30 s equilibration.

steps.title: Incorporate protein and incubate
steps.instruction: Introduce the purified membrane protein (detergent‑solubilized) into the destabilized liposomes.

substeps.instruction: Add the protein dropwise; keep the protein volume ≤10 % of the total liposome volume and test lipid‑to‑protein ratios of 1:20, 1:50, 1:100 or 1:200 (w/w).
Incubate the mixture for 15 min at room temperature with gentle stirring.
Include a negative control containing only purification buffer with detergent (no protein).

steps.title: Remove detergent with biobeads
steps.instruction: Adsorb detergent using Bio‑Beads SM‑2 in three sequential steps.

substeps.instruction: Add 200 mg Bio‑Beads per 5 mL reconstitution; stir 30 min at room temperature.
Add another 200 mg; stir 1 h at 4 °C.
Add a third 200 mg; stir overnight at 4 °C.
Next day add a fourth 200 mg; stir 2 h at 4 °C.

steps.title: Harvest and store proteoliposomes
steps.instruction: Separate the proteoliposomes from the beads, concentrate them, and store for future use.

substeps.instruction: Remove Bio‑Beads with a gravity‑flow column fitted with a filter.
Pellet the proteoliposomes by centrifugation at 240 000 × g for 40 min at 22 °C (MLA55 or Ti70 rotor).
Resuspend the pellet in storage buffer to 40 mg/mL.
Aliquot, flash‑freeze in liquid nitrogen, and store at –80 °C (extrude before freezing if desired).

steps.title: Prepare metal‑ion assay liposomes
steps.instruction: Combine proteoliposomes with fluorophore‑containing buffer and generate uniform vesicles for metal‑ion transport measurements.

substeps.instruction: Add ~1 mg lipids (as proteoliposomes) to 400 µL Buffer IN with fluorophore in a 2 mL Eppendorf tube.
Freeze‑thaw the mixture three times (liquid N₂ freeze, room‑temperature thaw); keep fluorophores protected from light.
Assemble the extruder, wash first with Buffer IN then with Buffer IN containing the fluorophore.
Load the sample and extrude 9–11 times through a 400 nm filter; rinse the extruder with 500 µL Buffer IN with fluorophore and add the rinse to the sample.

steps.title: Extrude and wash assay liposomes
steps.instruction: Pellet the extruded liposomes and perform two washes to remove external fluorophore.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge at 170 000 × g for 25 min at 22 °C using a TLA 100.3 rotor (≈900 µL total volume).
Carefully discard the supernatant and gently resuspend the pellet in 800 µL Buffer IN (cut the tip of a P1000 pipette to avoid shear).
Centrifuge again under the same conditions; repeat the wash once more for a total of two washes.

steps.title: Resuspend assay liposomes to stock concentration
steps.instruction: Adjust the final liposome concentration for the transport assay.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend the final pellet in 40 µL Buffer IN to obtain a stock of 0.25 mg/mL.

steps.title: Prepare proton‑transport assay liposomes
steps.instruction: Generate a proteoliposome stock suitable for ACMA‑based proton transport measurements.

substeps.instruction: Adjust the proteoliposome suspension to 15 mg/mL in 5 mM HEPES pH 7.0, 100 mM KCl, 50 µM ACMA (either by direct dilution or by the wash steps described in steps A5‑A7; add ACMA in the final resuspension).

steps.title: Sonicate proteoliposomes for proton assay
steps.instruction: Produce small unilamellar vesicles by sonication.

substeps.instruction: Place ~50 µL of the 15 mg/mL proteoliposome suspension in a glass tube (FIOLAX test tube).
Sonicate in a bath set to 80 V for 30–60 s with short breaks until the solution becomes optically clear.
Briefly centrifuge at room temperature to collect any droplets at the bottom; the supernatant is the liposome stock.

steps.title: Set up fluorescence measurement
steps.instruction: Dilute liposome stock, load plate, and configure the plate reader.

substeps.instruction: Dilute the liposome stock ~100‑fold by adding 8 µL stock to 830 µL Buffer OUT.
Dispense 100 µL of this dilution into each well of a 96‑well black‑walled plate (up to eight conditions).
Program the plate reader (e.g., Tecan Infinite M100) to record fluorescence continuously every 4 s for up to 360 cycles (24 min).

Select excitation/emission settings according to the fluorophore: Calcein (ex 492 nm/em 518 nm), Fura‑2 (ex 340 nm/em 510 nm and ex 380 nm/em 510 nm for ratio), Magnesium Green (ex 506 nm/em 531 nm), ACMA (ex 412 nm/em 482 nm).

steps.title: Add reagents during measurement
steps.instruction: Introduce membrane potential, substrate, and positive‑control ionophore while recording.

substeps.instruction: Baseline: record 60–90 cycles (~4–6 min) to obtain a stable fluorescence baseline.
Add 1 µL valinomycin stock to each well to generate a negative membrane potential; continue recording 20–30 cycles (~1.5–2 min).
Add 1 µL of the appropriate metal‑ion stock (Mn²⁺, Ca²⁺ or Mg²⁺) to start transport; record 75–270 cycles (5–18 min) depending on experimental goals.
Add 1 µL of the corresponding ionophore (Calcimycin for Mn²⁺/Mg²⁺, Ionomycin for Ca²⁺, CCCP for protons) as a positive control; record 10–20 cycles (1–1.5 min).
Use a programmable multichannel pipette: after each 1 µL addition, wash the tip with 1.5 µL of sample, change tips between additions, and mix 3–5 times with 50 µL. Avoid air bubbles.

steps.title: Analyze fluorescence data
steps.instruction: Process the recorded traces to obtain transport rates and kinetic parameters.

substeps.instruction: Normalize each trace to the fluorescence value at the time of substrate addition (or to the F340/F380 ratio for Fura‑2).
Identify the linear portion of the signal change (≈0.7 min after substrate addition) and perform linear regression to obtain initial transport velocity.
Fit velocities versus substrate concentration to the Michaelis–Menten equation to extract Kₘ and Vₘₐₓ.
Confirm assay integrity by verifying the maximal fluorescence increase after ionophore addition (positive control) and the lack of signal in protein‑free liposome controls.

description: Validation of protocol For each experimental condition, at least two independent proteoliposome reconstitutions have been analyzed, and at least three independent biological replicates were performed. The respective number of replicates is stated in the figure legends of the research articles listed below. Positive controls included known metal ion transporters with well characterized transport properties (EcoDMT in most cases, Figure 3A and C) and the addition of ionophores such as Calcimycin, Ionomycin, or CCCP to assess maximum fluorescence signals. Negative controls consisted of protein-free liposomes (data displayed in black in Figure 3B and D). Further validation of the assay can be provided by unrelated membrane proteins, inactive transporters due to point mutations, or specific inhibitors. This supports the conclusion that the observed signal arises from protein-mediated transport rather than passive leakage driven by the chemical gradient or membrane potential. This protocol (or parts of it) has been used and validated in the following research articles: Ehrnstorfer et al.
